description:
FOUND s484c (Opus, 2026-09-14) while reading #1727's probe rows 12-13, and
isolated with scratch/s484c/probe/p-io-slot.pl.  PRE-EXISTING.

perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    open(FH, '<', '/etc/hostname');
    *FH{IO}                 perl ref     PCL ref      agree
    *$g{IO}  ($g = \*FH)    perl ref     PCL ref      agree
    *STDOUT{IO}             perl ref     PCL ref      agree
    *NOPE{IO}               perl undef   PCL undef    agree
    close FH;  *FH{IO}      perl ref     PCL undef    <-- diverges

perl's `close` closes the IO object; it does not remove the glob's IO slot, so
`*FH{IO}` is still a ref (an IO::Handle on a closed handle) afterwards.  PCL's
IO slot IS the *p-filehandles* registration (`%p-resolve-fh`), and close
removes the registration, so the slot vanishes with the stream.

CONSEQUENCE: the Test.pm idiom `$TESTOUT = *STDOUT{IO}` is unaffected (nothing
closes STDOUT), which is why this has not surfaced; a program that closes a
handle and then asks whether the glob HAS an IO slot gets the wrong answer,
and so does `defined *FH{IO}` used as "was this ever opened".

FIX SHAPE (untried): distinguish "no IO slot" from "a CLOSED IO slot".  The
handle-value question is #220's (what a closed handle reads as), and this is
its introspection half, so read that task first â the cheapest shape is for
close to leave a CLOSED marker in *p-filehandles* rather than remhash it, with
every read path already having to answer "closed" anyway.

BAR: the five rows above, `print FH` after close still failing with EBADF
(the behaviour the deregistration currently gives, probed in
%p-glob-clear-io-slot's docstring), `undef *FH` still making the slot undef
(#1020's row 3), and the io/ companion leg.
subject: `*FH{IO}` is undef after `close FH` where perl keeps the slot â close DEREGISTERS the handle instead of closing it in place
